$comment: The backend's visibility provider vocabulary, committed so the frontend can be
tested against it (SIGV2-1163 follow-up: the frontend keyed Meta as `meta_ai`,
which the backend has never sent, so a real `meta` row missed the label map, the
logo map and the chart colour).
The backend is the contract. This file is a copy of it, not a second source of
truth, and it is kept in step by a test on each side:
- backend/tests/test_visibility_provider_contract.py asserts
SUPPORTED_VISIBILITY_PROVIDERS, VISIBILITY_PROVIDER_LABELS,
LIVE_MEASURABLE_PROVIDERS and the per-plan allowed_providers match this file,
so adding a provider to the backend fails backend CI until it is recorded here.
- frontend/src/types/monitoring.providerContract.test.ts asserts the frontend's
VisibilityProvider key set, VISIBILITY_PROVIDER_LABELS and the trend chart's
colour map cover exactly these keys, so recording a new provider here fails
frontend CI until the frontend handles it.
Neither test can pass while the two sides disagree, which is the point.
`labels` are the BACKEND's labels (the consumer engine each slot measures).
Since SIGV2-1161 the frontend's VISIBILITY_PROVIDER_LABELS shows these same
strings - the approved design uses consumer engine names only - so the
frontend contract test compares the label STRINGS as well as the keys.
`providers` is the VOCABULARY: every key a measurement has ever been recorded
under. `offered` is the subset the product actually offers and measures, and
`withdrawn` records why a key is in one list but not the other (SIGV2-1215).
A withdrawn key keeps its label and its recorded rows, and no customer
surface on either side may render it.
`plans` is VISIBILITY_PLAN_LIMITS: each plan's engine roster and its two sweep
cadences in seconds (the project's own domain, and its competitors, which are
separate dials since SIGV2-1208). Recorded here for SIGV2-1229, because copy
that states how often a number refreshes is a claim about that number's
freshness: the competitor gate still said "updated daily" after SIGV2-1208
moved the competitor sweep to weekly. A frontend test now derives the word
from these seconds instead of trusting a literal, so changing a cadence in the
backend fails the test that owns the sentence describing it.
`competitor_sweep_interval_seconds` is null on a plan that does not schedule
competitor measurement at all; those plans refresh competitors on demand only.
